text:
alex: Ran focused profiling on the TRT engine invoke path with vLLM scheduler tonight. Captured nsys (cuda,cudnn,osrt) + perfetto for single-request and B=8 batching. Perfetto link: https://perfetto.local/r/abc123 (internal).

mike: Quick highlights from the nsys summary: total avg latency ~120ms per request. Breakdown (approx): engine kernels 78ms, host memcpy H2D 18ms, wrapper/sync overhead 9ms, scheduler queuing/spin 9ms, postprocessing ~6ms.

priya: Interesting — wrapper/sync shows up as a contiguous CPU block just before the engine enqueue in the timeline, right? NVTX ranges would help slice that. Are we seeing any cudaDeviceSynchronize or implicit sync in the wrapper?

alex: Yes, timeline shows a 7-12ms host stall right before the engine kernel burst. No explicit cudaDeviceSynchronize in our code, but the TRT API calls into cuBLAS/cuDNN and there are small sync points. I also noticed repeated small H2D memcpy calls when KV cache miss happens. KV cache hit traces skip the copy and latency drops by ~25%.

mike: Kernel timeline: a tight burst of many tiny kernels (layernorm, attention_qk, gelu) from TRT between 10–80ms of the engine window. nvprof-style name aggregation shows many tiny kernels with lots of kernel launch overhead. That explains why batching helps but wrapper overhead adds fixed cost.

perf-bot: automatic-summary: engine_kernels=65%, host_overhead=10%, memcpy=15%, scheduler=8%, variance=B=8 +-4ms. (run-id: prof-1769999999) :eyes:

sophia: Two actionable experiments: 1) re-run with pinned (page-locked) host buffers to see if H2D drops; 2) add NVTX+trt profiler ranges around our wrapper and scheduler enqueue so we can separate enqueue latency vs kernel runtime. Also try concatenating small kernels into fused/custom kernels if possible.

priya: Also try disabling the thin vLLM wrapper layer (call TRT engine directly) to measure pure wrapper cost. If wrapper adds ~9ms we should try inline enqueue path or reduce roundtrips.

alex: Agreed. I'll queue three runs: (A) pinned host memory + nvtx ranges, (B) direct TRT invoke bypassing wrapper, (C) B=8 vs B=1 with kvcache cold/hot. I'll attach nsys commands I used: `nsys profile -t cuda,cudnn,osrt --output /tmp/prof-trt-1769999999 --capture-range=cudaProfilerApi ./run_invoke_test --batch=1` — similar for batch=8.

mike: One more micro-optimization idea: avoid host staging copies on KV cache hits by passing device pointers for cache frames; currently wrapper does H2D copy on every request for simplicity. If we can pin and only copy on miss, we cut that 18ms chunk frequently.

perf-bot: note: created ticket PERF-4123 to track: "reduce host-stage memcopies for KV cache hits". auto-linked traces: /traces/prof-1769999999.

alex: Good. I'll run A/B/C tomorrow morning and post perfetto slices + annotated screenshots. If pinned memory reduces memcpy by >50%, we push quick patch. Thanks all. :rocket:
